entries.teaser: An agent with a Gmail or Calendar connector can do things the platform cannot undo; a journal of every call, replayed, shows what it did and what can go back.
ideas: A connector is a grant of action
The platform keeps no way back for some actions
The twin is not a copy of the mailbox

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: The future of news is the story vault, not the paywall
entries.teaser: A story is a graph of claims and evidence and the article is one projection of it; keep the graph in a vault and sell what the article was made from.
ideas: Both models are bad for the reader
The story is a graph, the article is a projection
Anonymous sources are marked at the node

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: For a startup, the most important question is whether they miss it
entries.teaser: Ship something usable, give it away briefly, take it away and see whether anybody misses it; charge at a profit before you talk to investors.
ideas: Charge, and charge at a profit

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: The SaaS apocalypse will be decided by inertia, not by AI
entries.teaser: Incumbents and newcomers have the same AI; what separates them is how much past success each has to protect, so inertia decides which SaaS companies survive.
ideas: The claim, stated so it can be wrong
AI is available to both sides

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: Fractal Semantic Graphs: everything connects to everything, and nobody has to share a schema
entries.teaser: A fractal semantic graph has no privileged level and no single schema: each world keeps its own vocabulary and connects to others through named edges.

entries.author: sgit.ai
entries.title: The proof moved up, the homepage after the rebuild, next to the before pictures
entries.teaser: The rebuilt homepage puts four real vaults under one sentence, picks six by the job they do, and computes its numbers at build time from the site's own data.
ideas: The homepage as a view over data

entries.author: sgit.ai
entries.title: The proof is two clicks behind the claim, what the homepage gets wrong, and the fix
entries.teaser: The homepage leads with encryption, which cannot be seen, while twenty-five vaults a stranger can open in one click sit two clicks away in a table.
ideas: Encryption is a property you cannot look at
The proof is a table, two clicks away

entries.author: sgit.ai
entries.title: A chat box on a site with no server, the plan, and the trade it makes
entries.teaser: sgit.ai has no server, so its directory chat runs a local matcher by default, takes your own key as an opt-in, and leaves the vault bridge unbuilt.
ideas: A reader should never have to hold a credential to use an index
The bridge protects your key, not all egress

entries.author: sgit.ai
entries.title: Twenty sites in fifteen days, and what that did to the writing
entries.teaser: One site became twenty repositories in fifteen days because each argument needed its own version history, and the index now starts from a question.

entries.author: sgit.ai
entries.title: Git for things you cannot put on GitHub
entries.teaser: sgit is git for files you cannot put on GitHub: encrypted before they leave your machine, versioned like git, stored where the server cannot read a byte.

entries.author: sgit.ai
entries.title: Seven vaults, one method
entries.teaser: Publishing seven encrypted vaults in a fortnight produced a method, and every rule in it exists because something went wrong first.

entries.author: sgit.ai
entries.title: Green does not mean live
entries.teaser: Two releases passed every check and never reached the site because the checks stopped at the git remote; a release now ends by asking the live site its version.
ideas: The most likely thing to break is not your code
Shipped is a fact about the reader

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: The reader's own newsroom: a passkey that opens a vault, a vault that crosses browsers, and what a reader does once their reading is theirs
entries.teaser: From a design on 11 October to a vault every page can open, and what changes once your reading is yours to keep.
ideas: The passkey is a lock, not an identity
A signal the site engineered is not a signal
The modes are ways in, not replacements

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: No server, by design: a newsroom that runs in your browser, a model in the tab, and the agents that read, test and draw for it
entries.teaser: All the logic in the reader's browser, the keys and the model that make it possible, and the agents that read, test and draw for it.
ideas: No servers of mine with logic in them
Keep the meaning in the data, not in the prompt
A gap is a missing edge, and a missing edge is a query

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: Authority outside the model: Satya Nadella on models as insider risks, the platforms that now enforce, and the controls we run on our own agents
entries.teaser: An agent's limits only hold if they sit outside the agent. What that takes, from the platform to the daily routine.
ideas: A control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include
An agent must not be the one that decides its own limits
A rule kept by the agent it governs is hope

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: Pay after you read: a newsroom that charges for the share you read, lets you go below zero, and keeps your persona
entries.teaser: A newsroom you pay after you read, that never nags, and builds a persona that is yours.
ideas: You pay after you see the value
Going below zero is not a failure state
The reader should pay because paying helps them

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: How agents decide, when they stop, and a local story kept as evidence
entries.teaser: What a real decision needs, why agents do not stop by themselves, and who enforces each rule.
ideas: A yes or no is not agency
An entity that can go anywhere has no reason to stop
Every policy has a rule for everything; the difference is who enforces it

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: A team of agents, written up from the inside, and an open framework built on the same day
entries.teaser: Letting agents do real work for a business: how the team runs, what the policy really holds, and what it takes to trust them.
ideas: One story, three depths: an agent team from walkthrough to production
An open AI governance framework, turned into a vault the same day
A model that can go in every direction needs someone with a direction

entries.author: Dinis Cruz
entries.title: Get the next issue of the SGit Newsroom
entries.teaser: One issue a week or so: what was published, what it adds up to, and what is worth your time.
ideas: The week's articles, grouped by what they are about
Every quote checked word for word against its article
Next: an issue picked for what you care about
